top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single credited writer) best meets the common criteria on the evidence available: an unmistakable voice, formal ambition matched by control in Blinding and Solenoid, and a project that appears cumulative from lyric poetry through the large prose. The citation is narrowed to prose rooted in poetry, with no lineage or lifetime claims. Reservations remain: his effect lies in Romanian sentence rhythm that I can judge only through translation and critical report, and I cannot confirm that later volumes extend rather than repeat the earlier project. Maximalism is not depth, and the breadth of an inward mode is contested. These limits apply equally to any language-bound candidate and do not make no award preferable to a defensible single laureate. I do not count round-1 unanimity as merit, and I have not independently verified any source.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; my work as a DN critic and as a novelist of Central European history is context only and records no tie to Cărtărescu
